window-function.def: A function computed over a set of rows related to the current row, written with OVER. Unlike GROUP BY, every row stays.

partition-by.def: Splits the rows into groups inside OVER. The window function restarts for each partition, and no rows are collapsed.

row-number.def: Numbers rows 1, 2, 3 in the window's order, with no ties. Tied rows get different numbers, in no promised order.

dense-rank.def: Both give tied rows the same number. RANK then skips numbers, like 5, 5, 7; DENSE_RANK doesn't, like 5, 5, 6.

top-n-per-group.def: Number rows within each group with ROW_NUMBER, then keep numbers 1 to N in an outer query, since WHERE runs before window functions.

running-total.def: SUM over the rows so far, in order: SUM(x) OVER (ORDER BY day). Each row shows the total up to and including it.

lag.def: Read a value from the previous row, or the next one, in the window's order. The first row's LAG is NULL.

lines.hook.1: GROUP BY squeezes each group into one row. Sometimes you want to keep every row, with the group's number beside it.
lines.hook.2: Each product next to its category's average. Each order ranked. A running total, day by day.
lines.hook.3: That's what window functions do. Every row stays.
lines.goals.intro: Here's what you'll be able to do by the end of this lesson.
lines.goals.1: One. Put a group's number beside every row with OVER and PARTITION BY, and tell a window from a GROUP BY.
lines.goals.2: Two. Rank rows with ROW_NUMBER, RANK and DENSE_RANK, and return the top N per group.
lines.goals.3: Three. Build running totals, and compare a row with the one before it, using ORDER BY inside the window and LAG.
lines.over.1: Here are the eight products, with their categories.
lines.over.2: GROUP BY category gives three rows, one per category. The products are gone.
lines.over.3: AVG of price, OVER, partition by category, keeps all eight rows, and writes each category's average beside every product.
lines.over.4: A function with OVER is a <k id="window-function">window function</k>. <k id="partition-by">PARTITION BY</k> splits the rows into groups, without collapsing them.
lines.avg.1: Your turn. Show each product's name, category and price, with its category's average price beside it.
lines.avg.ask: Add the window function to the SELECT.

avg.hint.caption: AVG(price) OVER (PARTITION BY category)
avg.hint.voice: Average of price, over, partition by category.

lines.avg.error: The database couldn't run that. Check the brackets after OVER.
lines.avg.extra: Too many rows. There should be one per product.
lines.avg.missing: Rows or averages are off. Partition by category, and don't add a GROUP BY.
lines.avg.columns: Four columns: name, category, price, and the average.
lines.avg.done: Eight rows, every product kept. Compare with the correlated subquery from last time: same numbers, one pass.
lines.rank.1: Now ranking. Here are the products by units sold. Carrot cake and cinnamon roll are tied, at four each.
lines.rank.2: <k id="row-number">ROW_NUMBER</k> numbers the rows one, two, three. The tie gets two different numbers, in no promised order.
lines.rank.3: RANK gives the tie the same number, five and five, then skips to seven.
lines.rank.ask: Lemon tart comes after the tie. What does DENSE_RANK give it?
lines.rank.seven: That's RANK. DENSE_RANK doesn't skip, so it's six.
lines.rank.five: Five is the tie. Lemon tart comes next: six.
lines.rank.4: <k id="dense-rank">RANK and DENSE_RANK</k>: the same number for a tie, with or without a gap after it. Interviewers ask this one a lot.
lines.top.1: A classic: the most expensive product in each category.
lines.top.2: ROW_NUMBER, partitioned by category and ordered by price, descending. Each category counts from one again.
lines.top.3: Now keep row number one. But WHERE can't see it: window functions are computed after WHERE.
lines.top.4: So number the rows in a CTE, and filter in the outer query. That's <k id="top-n-per-group">top N per group</k>.
lines.top2.1: Your turn. The two most expensive products in each category.
lines.top2.ask: Finish the window function, then filter the numbered rows.

top2.hint.caption: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS rn, then WHERE rn <= 2.
top2.hint.voice: Row number, over, partition by category, order by price descending, as r n. Then keep r n up to two.

lines.top2.error: The database couldn't run that. Is the window function inside the CTE?
lines.top2.extra: Too many rows. Keep row numbers one and two.
lines.top2.missing: Some products are missing. Partition by category, and order by price, descending.
lines.top2.done: Six products, two per category. Top N per group, done.
lines.run.1: Window functions can also look back along the rows. Here's the bakery's revenue, day by day.
lines.run.2: SUM of revenue, over, order by day. Each row adds itself to everything before it.

run.3.caption: That's a running total. By the 25th it reaches 161.25.
run.3.voice: That's a running total. By the twenty-fifth, it reaches a hundred and sixty-one twenty-five.

lines.lag.1: And LAG reads the previous row. Here are Maya's four orders.
lines.lag.2: LAG of ordered at puts her previous order's date beside each one. Her first order has none, so it's NULL.
lines.lag.3: Subtract, and you get the gaps: three days, seven, then thirteen. Maya's slowing down.
lines.lag.4: <k id="lag">LAG and LEAD</k> read the row before or after. Handy for gaps, changes and streaks.
lines.gap.1: Last one. For each of Maya's orders, show the date of her previous order.

gap.hint.caption: LAG(ordered_at) OVER (ORDER BY ordered_at)
gap.hint.voice: Lag of ordered at, over, order by ordered at.

lines.gap.error: The database couldn't run that. Check the brackets after OVER.
lines.gap.extra: Too many rows. Only Maya's orders: customer one.
lines.gap.missing: Some rows or dates are off. Order the window by the order date.
lines.gap.columns: Three columns: the order's ID, its date, and the previous date.
lines.gap.done: Four orders, and the first has no previous one. That's LAG.
lines.recap.intro: Let's look back at what you can do now.
lines.recap.1: A window function works over a group but keeps every row. Eight products in, eight rows out, each with its category's average.
lines.recap.2: Ties share a rank. RANK leaves a gap after them, DENSE_RANK doesn't. For top N per group, number the rows in a CTE, then filter outside.
lines.recap.3: With ORDER BY inside the window, SUM becomes a running total, and LAG reads the row before. Maya's first order has no previous one.
lines.check.intro: Now three quick checks. Each asks you to use an idea, not just name it.

check.q1.caption: COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY category) on 8 products in 3 categories. How many rows come back?
check.q1.voice: Count star, over, partition by category, on eight products in three categories. How many rows come back?

lines.check.q1-why: Eight. A window function never removes rows. Each product gets its category's count beside it.
lines.check.q2: Four prices, from high to low: six fifty, five ninety, five ninety, two eighty. What does each function give the two eighty?
lines.check.q2-why: ROW_NUMBER just counts, so four. RANK gives the tie two and two, then skips to four. DENSE_RANK doesn't skip, so three.

check.q3.caption: A running total of daily revenue: SUM(revenue) OVER ( ? ). What goes in the brackets?
check.q3.voice: A running total of daily revenue: the sum of revenue, over what?

lines.check.q3-why: ORDER BY day. It lines the days up, so each row adds itself to everything before it. PARTITION BY day would restart every day.

check.pass.caption: {right} / 3. The ideas are sticking.
check.pass.voice: Nicely done. The ideas are sticking.

check.retry.caption: {right} / 3. The goals marked revisit are the ones to replay.
check.retry.voice: A few to revisit. The goals marked revisit at the end are the ones to replay.

lines.interview.intro: Now an interview round. Two quick questions, then one you answer in your own words.

interview.w1.caption: What's the difference between ROW_NUMBER, RANK and DENSE_RANK?
interview.w1.speaker: interviewer

lines.interview.w1-why: They only differ on ties. ROW_NUMBER breaks them arbitrarily, RANK leaves a gap after them, and DENSE_RANK doesn't.

interview.w2.caption: When would you use a window function instead of GROUP BY?
interview.w2.speaker: interviewer

lines.interview.w2-why: When you need the group's value beside each row. GROUP BY collapses the group; a window keeps every row.

interview.open.caption: Find the top three customers by total spend in each city. Walk me through the query, and tell me what happens with ties.
interview.open.speaker: interviewer

lines.finish.1: That's the lesson. Window functions keep every row. PARTITION BY groups them, ORDER BY lines them up, and ranks, totals and LAG read along the line.
